clue.text: Big money, cigars … not one involved in this

definitions.text: Big money, cigars … not one involved in this

indicators.note: letters that are involved are tangled together, so the fodder words are mixed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sneer at a working world where nobody on the ground sees big money or celebratory cigars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles BIG MONEY, CIGARS, NOT and I (one). The whole clue also describes the answer: in this economy of casual work, nobody gets big money and cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the UK labour market of short freelance jobs, where few workers earn fortunes, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Books turned up in seconds, one after the other

indicators.note: in tells us the turned letters sit inside the doubled word for seconds

parts.note: to second is to back a proposal, so seconds gives two backs

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters for books are read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pile of books upended within moments, in quick succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the letters for books, and 'in' sets them in the middle. To second a motion is to back it, so 'seconds' is two backers side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Events happening consecutively, with no gap between them, are said to come in an unbroken row.

clue.text: Hosts banquets, taking quick look round inside — Duke's not there!

indicators.note: taking says the banquet word takes another piece into itself
inside confirms the reversed look goes within the other word
not there says the letter for Duke is missing from the banquets

parts.note: dinners are banquets or formal meals
D is the abbreviation for Duke; the 's is just 'is'

indicators.note: round says the quick look is turned back to front

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Banquet hosts glance about the room only to find the Duke has not turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not there' leaves INNERS; 'round' turns the look back to front, and 'taking ... inside' sets it after INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords of pubs or inns receive and serve guests, so they are hosts in the hospitality sense.

clue.text: Free bar — I'm full to capacity

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the word bar are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: the word I'm gives its letters with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A free bar means the pub is packed to the rafters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges BAR into ABR, followed by IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel filled right to its edge is full up, a literary word for brimming.

clue.text: Required to stop poverty, no end to sick state's failing

indicators.note: to stop means the scrambled letters plug the middle of the poverty word

parts.note: need is poverty or want

indicators.note: failing suggests something going wrong, so these letters are disordered
no end to means the final letter of the word sick is dropped

parts.note: the word state supplies its own letters; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A call for action to end poverty, as an ailing state lets its people down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end to' leaves SIC; 'failing' scrambles it with the state letters, and 'to stop' plugs the result into the middle of the poverty word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was made unavoidable or compulsory by circumstances was required, a past-tense verb either way.

clue.text: Peace and love? Left first to cut through pretence

indicators.note: to cut through means the pair of letters slices into the pretence word

parts.note: a sham is a pretence

indicators.note: first says the letter for left comes before the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hippie-ish slogan, with a political turn to the left breaking through the fakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts L ahead of O, and 'to cut through' places LO inside SHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word of greeting and farewell literally means peace.

clue.text: Greeting Henry with hot drink outside

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
and means with or together with

indicators.note: outside means the drink wraps round the letter for hot

parts.note: sake is Japanese rice wine
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone greets Henry by offering him a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps SAKE round H to give SHAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and pumping hands is a common physical way to greet someone.

clue.text: Remain in Mulholland Drive?

definitions.meaning: to remain is to go on or endure
Mulholland Drive is a Los Angeles street

explanation.surface: A wish to stay on in the famous road above Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the letters as LA ST, an abbreviated Los Angeles street; the question mark flags that it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or hold out over time is the verb sense; the address abbreviation names a street in Los Angeles.

clue.text: Jennifer finally leaving as Johnson was dressing

indicators.note: leaving says the chosen letter departs from the word

parts.note: Boris Johnson was Mayor of London before becoming Prime Minister

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the name Jennifer

explanation.surface: Jennifer has gone, and Boris Johnson was dressing as she left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from Jennifer, and 'leaving' removes it from MAYOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name for mayonnaise, a creamy sauce or salad dressing.

clue.text: See 22
Wife's getting frisky with actor on Peaky — not a good one

indicators.note: frisky letters are playful and lively, so the fodder is jumbled

explanation.surface: A wife makes a pass at an actor from Peaky Blinders, the BBC gangster drama, which is not good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting frisky' rearranges WIFES, ACTOR, ON and PEAKY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an unpleasant, untrustworthy person, so 'not a good one' fits.

clue.text: Guardian's German writer taking one in (as I do here)

parts.note: a parent is a guardian; the 's is just 'has'

indicators.note: taking says the writer's name takes another letter into itself
in confirms the letter for one goes within the writer's name

parts.note: Hermann Hesse was a German-born novelist
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A newspaper, the Guardian, claims a German author, with an aside in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... in' places I inside HESSE to give HESISE. The definition works because the clue itself sets 'as I do here' in brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting words in brackets as an aside is exactly what the setter does with the final phrase.

clue.text: Herbert's story entertains a majority of regulators

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in or hold, so the novel's title holds the other piece

parts.note: The Rats is a 1974 horror novel by James Herbert
most means the greater part, a majority

explanation.surface: A tale by someone named Herbert amuses most of the people who make the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' puts MOST inside THE RATS, splitting it after THE R.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating devices that switch on and off to hold a set temperature are regulators of a system.

clue.text: See 1 across
Strange about a king turning into stone

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: into says the turned pair goes inside the stone word

parts.note: marble is a type of stone

indicators.note: turning means the letters for a and king are read the other way round

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: An odd story of a king being turned to stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes KA, which goes 'into' the stone after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary or worthy of comment is unusual, which matches strange.

clue.text: Exercise in order for man?

indicators.note: in says the exercise letters sit within the order word

parts.note: a bid is an order or command, as in 'do my bidding'
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a man needs exercise to keep him in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'man' as an example: humans are one kind of two-legged animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-footed animal; a man is one example, hence the query in the clue.

clue.text: Poor shot selection at start splits Mark's supporters in opening frame

indicators.note: splits says the other letters break into the middle of the mark word

parts.note: a dot is a mark, and the 's adds an S to make dots

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of poor are scrambled
at start picks only the opening letter of the word selection

explanation.surface: A snooker or cricket report: a bad choice of shot early on costs Mark in the opening frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles the letters of poor into ORPO, 'at start' adds S, and 'splits' breaks the mark word after two letters. 'shot selection' and 'frame' are sporting misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright side pieces of a door frame hold the door up, so they are its supporters.

clue.text: Queen stage musical review — initially it's repetitious

indicators.note: initially says the word it comes at the very front

parts.note: the word it gives its own letters; the 's is just 'is'
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

indicators.note: read as re-view, it means look at the musical again from the other end

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical about Eva Peron

explanation.surface: A critic's take on a Queen musical on stage: from the start it repeats itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' turns the musical round, 'initially' puts IT at the front. Queen the rock band, whose songs fill a stage musical, is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A process that repeats the same step over and over is repetitive, a near synonym.

clue.text: Bird (Romeo's second) managed to break bed

indicators.note: to break means the inner letters force the bed word apart

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's is just 'has'
mo is short for moment, a second
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A bird got into Romeo's bed for a moment, in a scene with a whiff of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' splits the bed word before its last letter. Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet, and 'second' is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A large dark fish-eating seabird is one species of bird.

clue.text: Tame! Newcastle after setback having big clear-out

indicators.note: after setback says the hidden letters are read backwards
having means the two words hold the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A football fan begs Newcastle to calm down after a defeat that leads to a squad clear-out.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'having' as part of the definition, but the hidden word needs an indicator: 'having' says the words contain it, and 'after setback' turns it round. The noun 'big clear-out' then matches the noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectal flush that empties the bowels is a medical clear-out, a thorough purge of the system.

clue.text: See 10
She has nothing over Ruby

indicators.note: over means covering, so the nothing word goes round the colour

parts.note: FA is short for 'sweet FA', slang for nothing at all
ruby is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A woman has nothing over Ruby, so the two are equals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' wraps the nothing word round the colour. 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing at all, and ruby is a deep red.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so any bearer of it is a she.

clue.text: Variable working horror — cue to act over numbers initially on it?

definitions.text: Variable working horror — cue to act over numbers initially on it?

parts.note: Z is a standard algebraic variable

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked over into a new order
initially picks the opening letter of the word numbers

explanation.surface: A complaint about unpredictable hours: the dreaded call to work comes with no set number of hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Z (an algebra variable) comes first; 'working' scrambles HORROR, CUE, TO ACT and N, the first letter of 'numbers'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A UK employment arrangement guaranteeing no minimum hours, so workers wait for the call and the numbers on it vary.

clue.text: See 22
Selfish being last to come and first to leave

indicators.note: to says first is attached next to the leave word
last picks the closing letter of the word come

parts.note: to go is to leave
1ST is the abbreviation of first, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: Someone self-centred always turns up last and is the first to go.
explanation.walkthrough: E (last of 'come') leads; then GO with 1ST (first) put to it, the digit 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person who puts their own interests first is a selfish person, a noun like 'being'.

clue.text: Press release about bishop — it's explosive

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the press and release words run backwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd or press of people
to emit is to release or give out
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A press release about a bishop causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses MOBEMIT into TIMEBOM, before B. 'Press release' looks like one phrase but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A device set to detonate later is literally explosive, and the term also means a crisis waiting to happen.

clue.text: Maneater makes advance prince rejected?

indicators.note: rejected means the prince letters are thrown out of the word

parts.note: progress is advance or forward movement

explanation.surface: A predatory woman makes an advance that a prince turns down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' removes PR from PROGRESS. 'Maneater' here is literal: a female monster from fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A female giant of folklore who eats people is literally a man-eater.

clue.text: Developed at last the battery's storage capacity

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word battery supplies its letters; the 's is just 'has'

indicators.note: at last picks the closing letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Tech news: at last, a battery has been developed with huge storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes E from 'the', and 'Developed' scrambles it with BATTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of data equal to a trillion bytes measures how much a drive can store.
